findings.message: The torn orange trail-marker cloth found in gear-search-notice (picked up and pocketed 'just in case') is never referenced again; it is not tracked as an item and has no payoff. ending-1's 'bright patch of orange' is a separate search-team flag, not this cloth. Likewise the remembered marker direction in scout-ahead-notice ('that small fact might matter later') is never used. These read as loose threads for an attentive child reader. Not a blocker since no mechanic depends on them, but narrative-designer should either pay these off or remove the implication that they matter.

late-gear-find and late-clue-find largely re-describe the same scene and object in near-identical phrasing to gear-search and scout-ahead ('half buried in frost', 'the thin, dark crack line', 'the old deer track... might pass below the worst drop'). This is not a structural page revisit (no backward graph edge; these are distinct, newly-written passages, and the graph report confirms the route to every ending is a forward-only DAG with no re-reading of already-visited passages), but the heavy phrase reuse makes the second-look passages feel repetitive on a route that takes both.

Several choice pairs (wrap-snug/wrap-firm, pack-away/double-check, tell-group/study-more, mark-direction/hurry-on, check-russo-first/scan-ridge-first) converge on an identical next passage with no state effect or textual difference. Fine for pacing on a first read, but reduces the sense of agency on a reread; flagging for awareness, not required to fix.
